Ground mismatch: PHI are run-first (37% pass when leading) into a TEN front that bleeds 125 rush yds/game and 0.53 RB1 rushing scores. Saquon Barkley is a centerpiece — and the game script only feeds him.

The TEN welcome the PHI as underdogs of 4.5, with the total set at 42.5 — a market that implies a PHI 24–19 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 33% of its snaps with PHI in front, 42% within one score, and 25% with PHI chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

A modest edge to PHI. They should lead more often than not, tilting them slightly toward the run late, while TEN leans a touch more pass-heavy to stay in it — but the effect is gentle; this isn't a script that dramatically reshapes anyone's usage.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Tony Pollard — PHI are stingy against the run (112 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Sneaky value on Dontayvion Wicks (WR2) — TEN leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Sneaky value on Wan'Dale Robinson (WR2) — PHI leak 42 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Wan'Dale Robinson faces a tough cover — PHI hold WR1s to just 52 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Touchdown Board

Saquon Barkley is a bell-cow (77% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.53 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

DeVonta Smith carries TD equity — TEN surrender 0.53 WR1 receiving scores a game.

PHI pound it at the goal line (36% pass in the red zone) — Saquon Barkley owns the rushing-TD equity.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A modest lean to PHI — they should lead more often than not, nudging them toward the run late and giving Saquon Barkley a gentle game-script tailwind.

PHI — a run-heavy offense

PHI are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 37% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

This is the profile that most rewards a lead back. As a 4-point favorite projected to lead for 33% of snaps, PHI will be running to close the game, and their run-first identity compounds it. Saquon Barkley is the beneficiary — we project 15 carries for 68 yards, and his ceiling is where the value sits: in the simulations where this becomes a two-score game, his volume spikes as PHI salt it away.

The flip side: DeVonta Smith (6 targets, 53 yards) has his ceiling capped by the same script that helps the run game — when PHI lead and run, there simply aren't as many pass attempts to go around. He's a safer floor than ceiling play in this spot.

Underneath, Dallas Goedert (TE, 6 targets, 51 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

TEN — a run-heavy offense

TEN are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 38% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Game script works against the run here — TEN project to trail and throw, which squeezes Tony Pollard's rushing projection (14 carries, 63 yards) but raises his value as a receiver; trailing teams check the ball down, and his target share ticks up as the game gets away from them.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the one to target from a volume standpoint: as underdogs throwing to keep pace, TEN funnel work to their top receiver — 8 targets for 49 yards projected, with genuine upside if they fall behind early and the game turns one-dimensional.

Underneath, Gunnar Helm (TE, 3 targets, 23 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 4-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
